title: Isaiah 26 — The song of Judah and the dead who rise

verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed the MT: yᵉšûʿāh yāšîṯ ḥômôṯ wā-ḥēl is a genuine syntactic crux, and the ASV-aligned 'he sets salvation as walls and rampart' (salvation as the fortifying material, ḥēl the outer rampart) is squarely within the scholarly range, the JPS alternative being disclosed in the note. yûšar is correctly the passive 'shall be sung'.
Verified against MT: 'open the gates, that a righteous nation may enter, one that keeps faithfulness' renders pitḥû šᵉʿārîm … šōmēr ʾĕmunîm plainly; no divergence from consensus and no lens.

yēṣer sāmûḵ 'the steadfast mind' and tiṣṣōr 'you keep' parse correctly; preserving the doubled šālôm ׀ šālôm literally as 'peace, peace' (with the 'perfect peace' intensive disclosed in commentary) is a defensible literalism, not a lens move.

The unusual bᵉ-Yāh YHWH is handled by transliterating the short name 'Yah' distinct from the YHWH house-style, keeping the source's own juxtaposition visible; ṣûr ʿôlāmîm 'an everlasting rock' (lower-case epithet, durational ʿôlāmîm) is standard.
MT hēšaḥ … yašpîlennāh yašpîlāh … yaggîʿennāh parses as the doubling-for-emphasis 'brings low … lays it low … to the ground … to the dust'; rendered plainly, no lens.
tirmᵉsennāh rāgel … ʿānî … dallîm 'the foot tramples it — the feet of the poor, the steps of the weak' is verified against MT; consensus rendering.

Reading yāšār as a vocative divine epithet 'O Upright One' is JPS-attested and suits the running 2ms address to YHWH (26:8-12); the adjectival ('the path is straight', ASV) alternative is disclosed and the note explicitly commits no divine-identity lens. tᵉp̄allēs 'make level/smooth' is correct.
ʾōraḥ mišpāṭeḵā … qiwwînûḵā … taʾăwaṯ-nāp̄eš 'we have waited for you … the desire of the soul' verified against MT; standard rendering, no lens.
napšî ʾiwwîṯîḵā … ʾăšaḥărekkā (šḥr 'seek earnestly') and the judgments-teach-righteousness clause parse correctly; rendered plainly.
yuḥan rāšāʿ (Hophal 'be shown favor') … bᵉʾereṣ nᵉḵōḥôṯ 'in the land of uprightness' … gēʾûṯ YHWH 'the majesty of YHWH' verified; eretz correctly 'land' in this local sense, not forced cosmic.

rāmāh yāḏᵉḵā … qinʾaṯ-ʿām 'your zeal for the people' … ʾēš ṣāreḵā tōʾḵᵉlēm parses; the supplied 'kept for' in 'the fire kept for your adversaries' is a mild idiomatic expansion of the opaque construct ʾēš-ṣāreḵā and stays within the standard versional range, no lens.
tišpōṯ šālôm lānû 'you will establish peace for us' (špt 'set/ordain') and kol-maʿăśênû pāʿaltā lānû verified; standard.

KEY lens check: ʾĕlōhênû is correctly 'our God' — the 'the Elohim' convention is withheld from a suffixed first-person confession, consistent with the 53:4/24:15/25:1,9 precedent, and I confirmed the central elohim-as-translation entry carries NO ISA-26:13. ʾăḏōnîm zûlāṯeḵā is the plural of ʾāḏôn (human/foreign overlords), correctly NOT the divine title ʾăḏōnāy; no divine referent imported.

citations: J. Day, God's Conflict with the Dragon and the Sea (1985)
L'Heureux, Rank Among the Canaanite Gods (1979)
verdicts.reasoning: KEY lens check: rᵉp̄āʾîm here stands in parallel with mēṯîm 'the dead' and is unambiguously the Sheol-shades sense (H7496), correctly rendered 'the shades' — NOT the giant-Rephaim/Nephilim (H7497). I verified that neither the central refaim-giant-peoples nor nephilim-giants entry carries ISA-26:14; the giant-warrior homonym is confined to the overlay note. Scholarly consensus.
yāsap̄tā laggôy (doubled) … niḵbādtā … riḥaqtā kol-qaṣwê-ʾāreṣ 'you have increased the nation … extended far all the borders of the land' verified against MT; standard.

The colon ṣāqûn laḥaš is genuinely hard; deriving anomalous ṣāqûn from ṣûq 'pour out' and taking laḥaš as a hushed prayer ('they poured out a whispered prayer', JPS) over the charm/incantation sense is defensible, fits the baṣṣar/mûsār distress context, and the difficulty is flagged. No lens.
The parturition simile (hārāh … taqrîḇ lāleḏeṯ … tāḥîl tizʿaq baḥăḇālêhā) is rendered plainly and correctly; no divergence.

yāladnû rûaḥ 'we gave birth to wind' is correct; taking yippᵉlû (nāp̄al) as 'come to birth' in continuity with the birth-imagery (JPS, playing on nēp̄el 'stillbirth') over 'fallen/overthrown' (ASV) is a genuine versional option, disclosed in the note. This is the FAILED-labor foil of 26:19, so the reading carries no resurrection-lens pressure.

citations: J. Day, God's Conflict with the Dragon and the Sea (1985)
J. D. Levenson, Resurrection and the Restoration of Israel (2006)
verdicts.reasoning: MARQUEE verdict: the MT surface is rendered plainly — 'Your dead shall live; my corpses shall rise. Awake and sing … you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth will give birth to the shades.' yiḥyû mēṯeḵā is grammatically explicit. The number crux nᵉḇēlāṯî(1cs)/yᵉqûmûn(3mp) is rendered collectively 'my corpses' retaining MT against the nᵉḇēlāṯām emendation (the 1cs 'my' is preserved, not smoothed to 'their'); ṭal ʾôrōṯ 'dew of lights' (NRSV) is retained over the 'herbs' homograph, disclosed; tappîl 'give birth to' (NRSV) is within range with ASV 'cast forth' noted; rᵉp̄āʾîm again correctly 'shades'. The bodily-resurrection reading and the Dan 12:2/Ezek 37 cross-corpus cluster are confined to commentary and to the central resurrection entry, which I confirmed keeps the corporate/individual question open and routes the Raëlian reading to apparatus. No eschatological-program identification leaks into the English.

Both ketiv/qere pairs (dᵉlāṯeḵā/dᵉlāṯḵā 'doors/door'; yaʿăḇôr/yaʿăḇār 'passes') are handled per the project's qere-first structural-preservation rule — qere translated, ketiv preserved verbatim in text/he and noted; the differences are orthographic/morphological. ḥăḇî 'hide yourself', zaʿam 'indignation' correct. lēḵ rendered 'Come' (NRSV) is idiomatic and defensible.

The theophany YHWH yōṣēʾ mimmᵉqômô 'coming out from his place' (cf. Mic 1:3), lip̄qōḏ ʿăwōn 'to punish the iniquity', and the ground disclosing its absorbed blood (gillᵉṯāh … dāmehā; cf. Gen 4:10-11) are rendered plainly, no lens. ʿăwōn governed by the central avon keyword; I confirmed the central entry now carries ISA-26:21 (bare distribution addition, appropriate).

direct verified: yēṣer sāmûḵ 'steadfast mind' is lexically explicit and the literal preservation of the doubled šālôm is a defensible rendering choice with the intensive idiom disclosed.

direct verified: transliterating the short name Yāh distinct from YHWH and rendering ṣûr ʿôlāmîm 'everlasting rock' (lower-case epithet, durational plural) are grammatically explicit and consensus-consistent.

direct verified: the vocative 'O Upright One' is a genuine, JPS-attested construal of yāšār suiting the 2ms context; the adjectival alternative is disclosed and no divine-identity lens is committed, so 'direct' holds.

direct verified and lens-clean: ʾĕlōhênû 'our God' (elohim convention withheld, confirmed non-applied centrally) and ʾăḏōnîm 'other lords' as human overlords (not the divine ʾăḏōnāy) are both the standard ASV/JPS values.

Both central giant-people entries correctly carry no ISA-26 refs.
direct verified: the hushed-prayer reading of the hard colon ṣāqûn laḥaš matches JPS, fits the distress context, and the difficulty plus the charm/incantation alternative are honestly flagged.

paragraphs.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יוּשַׁ֥ר הַשִּׁיר־הַזֶּ֖ה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֑ה עִ֣יר עָז־לָ֔נוּ יְשׁוּעָ֥ה יָשִׁ֖ית חוֹמ֥וֹת וָחֵֽל׃

i18n.en: In that day this song shall be sung in the land of Judah: “We have a strong city; he sets salvation as walls and rampart.”
i18n.he: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יוּשַׁ֥ר הַשִּׁיר־הַזֶּ֖ה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֑ה עִ֣יר עָז־לָ֔נוּ יְשׁוּעָ֥ה יָשִׁ֖ית חוֹמ֥וֹת וָחֵֽל׃

notes.official: *Yᵉšûʿāh* 'salvation' is the crux of the opening song. The clause *yᵉšûʿāh yāšîṯ ḥômôṯ wā-ḥēl* can set salvation AS the city's walls and rampart (ASV 'salvation will he appoint for walls and bulwarks') or appoint walls and rampart FOR salvation (JPS 1917); this translation takes the former — YHWH's salvation is itself the fortification, *ḥēl* being the outer wall or fore-rampart (BDB, HALOT). The passive *yûšar* (Hophal of *šîr*) 'shall be sung' marks an eschatological hymn 'in that day', and the 'strong city' (*ʿîr ʿoz-lānû*) of salvation stands against the 'lofty city' brought down to the dust at 26:5 (Wildberger, *Isaiah 13–27*, 1997; Blenkinsopp, *Isaiah 1–39*, AB 19, 2000).

paragraphs.text: פִּתְח֖וּ שְׁעָרִ֑ים וְיָבֹ֥א גוֹי־צַדִּ֖יק שֹׁמֵ֥ר אֱמֻנִֽים׃

i18n.en: Open the gates, that a righteous nation may enter, one that keeps faithfulness.
i18n.he: פִּתְח֖וּ שְׁעָרִ֑ים וְיָבֹ֥א גוֹי־צַדִּ֖יק שֹׁמֵ֥ר אֱמֻנִֽים׃

paragraphs.text: יֵ֣צֶר סָמ֔וּךְ תִּצֹּ֖ר שָׁל֣וֹם ׀ שָׁל֑וֹם כִּ֥י בְךָ֖ בָּטֽוּחַ׃

i18n.en: The steadfast mind you keep in peace, peace, because it trusts in you.
i18n.he: יֵ֣צֶר סָמ֔וּךְ תִּצֹּ֖ר שָׁל֣וֹם ׀ שָׁל֑וֹם כִּ֥י בְךָ֖ בָּטֽוּחַ׃

notes.official: The doubled *šālôm ׀ šālôm* is preserved literally on the surface as 'peace, peace' rather than collapsed to the intensive idiom 'perfect peace' (KJV/ASV): the reduplication is an emphatic superlative-by-doubling, and keeping it lets the reader see the Hebrew's own emphasis. *Yēṣer sāmûḵ* is 'a steadfast / firmly-supported mind or purpose' — *yēṣer* the noun of formation and inclination (the same word as the *yēṣer* of Gen 6:5), *sāmûḵ* 'supported, sustained' — which YHWH keeps (*tiṣṣōr*) in that peace because it trusts in him (Wildberger; BDB, HALOT s.v. *yēṣer*).

paragraphs.text: בִּטְח֥וּ בַֽיהוָ֖ה עֲדֵי־עַ֑ד כִּ֚י בְּיָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה צ֖וּר עוֹלָמִֽים׃

i18n.en: Trust in YHWH for ever and ever, for in Yah YHWH is an everlasting rock.
i18n.he: בִּטְח֥וּ בַֽיהוָ֖ה עֲדֵי־עַ֑ד כִּ֚י בְּיָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה צ֖וּר עוֹלָמִֽים׃

notes.official: The short divine name *Yāh* (יָהּ, the shortened Tetragrammaton, as in *hallĕlû-Yāh*) is transliterated 'Yah' and kept distinct from the corpus 'YHWH' house-style for the full name, so the source's juxtaposition *bᵉ-Yāh YHWH* is visible rather than folded into 'the LORD is GOD' (JPS) or a repeated 'Jehovah, even Jehovah' (ASV). *Ṣûr ʿôlāmîm* 'an everlasting rock' deploys *ṣûr* 'rock' as a divine epithet (Deut 32:4, 18, 31; Isa 30:29; 2 Sam 22:2–3), rendered lower-case rather than capitalized as a fixed title; *ʿôlāmîm* (plural of *ʿôlām* 'far-distant time, age') is durational 'everlasting', not metaphysical eternity (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י הֵשַׁח֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י מָר֔וֹם קִרְיָ֖ה נִשְׂגָּבָ֑ה יַשְׁפִּילֶ֤נָּה יַשְׁפִּילָהּ֙ עַד־אֶ֔רֶץ יַגִּיעֶ֖נָּה עַד־עָפָֽר׃

i18n.en: For he has brought low those who dwell on high, the lofty city; he lays it low, lays it low to the ground, brings it down to the dust.
i18n.he: כִּ֤י הֵשַׁח֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י מָר֔וֹם קִרְיָ֖ה נִשְׂגָּבָ֑ה יַשְׁפִּילֶ֤נָּה יַשְׁפִּילָהּ֙ עַד־אֶ֔רֶץ יַגִּיעֶ֖נָּה עַד־עָפָֽר׃

paragraphs.text: תִּרְמְסֶ֖נָּה רָ֑גֶל רַגְלֵ֥י עָנִ֖י פַּעֲמֵ֥י דַלִּֽים׃

i18n.en: The foot tramples it — the feet of the poor, the steps of the weak.
i18n.he: תִּרְמְסֶ֖נָּה רָ֑גֶל רַגְלֵ֥י עָנִ֖י פַּעֲמֵ֥י דַלִּֽים׃

paragraphs.text: אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים יָשָׁ֕ר מַעְגַּ֥ל צַדִּ֖יק תְּפַלֵּֽס׃

i18n.en: The way of the righteous is level; O Upright One, you make smooth the path of the righteous.
i18n.he: אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים יָשָׁ֕ר מַעְגַּ֥ל צַדִּ֖יק תְּפַלֵּֽס׃

notes.official: *Yāšār* 'upright' is read as a vocative divine epithet — 'O Upright One, you make smooth the path of the righteous' (JPS 'Thou Most Upright') — rather than adjectivally of the path ('the way of the righteous is straight', ASV); the vocative suits the second-person address to YHWH running through 26:8–12, and no divine-identity lens is committed. *Tᵉp̄allēs* (Piel of *pālas* 'weigh out, make level') is 'you make level / smooth' — the path made straight and passable for the righteous (Wildberger; Kaiser, *Isaiah 13–39*, OTL, 1974).

paragraphs.text: אַ֣ף אֹ֧רַח מִשְׁפָּטֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה קִוִּינ֑וּךָ לְשִׁמְךָ֥ וּֽלְזִכְרְךָ֖ תַּאֲוַת־נָֽפֶשׁ׃

i18n.en: Yea, in the path of your judgments, O YHWH, we have waited for you; for your name and for your remembrance is the desire of the soul.
i18n.he: אַ֣ף אֹ֧רַח מִשְׁפָּטֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה קִוִּינ֑וּךָ לְשִׁמְךָ֥ וּֽלְזִכְרְךָ֖ תַּאֲוַת־נָֽפֶשׁ׃

paragraphs.text: נַפְשִׁ֤י אִוִּיתִ֙יךָ֙ בַּלַּ֔יְלָה אַף־רוּחִ֥י בְקִרְבִּ֖י אֲשַֽׁחֲרֶ֑ךָּ כִּ֞י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר מִשְׁפָּטֶ֙יךָ֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ צֶ֥דֶק לָמְד֖וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃

i18n.en: With my soul I have desired you in the night; yea, with my spirit within me I seek you earnestly; for when your judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
i18n.he: נַפְשִׁ֤י אִוִּיתִ֙יךָ֙ בַּלַּ֔יְלָה אַף־רוּחִ֥י בְקִרְבִּ֖י אֲשַֽׁחֲרֶ֑ךָּ כִּ֞י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר מִשְׁפָּטֶ֙יךָ֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ צֶ֥דֶק לָמְד֖וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃

paragraphs.text: יֻחַ֤ן רָשָׁע֙ בַּל־לָמַ֣ד צֶ֔דֶק בְּאֶ֥רֶץ נְכֹח֖וֹת יְעַוֵּ֑ל וּבַל־יִרְאֶ֖ה גֵּא֥וּת יְהוָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Though the wicked be shown favor, he does not learn righteousness; in the land of uprightness he deals wrongfully, and does not see the majesty of YHWH.
i18n.he: יֻחַ֤ן רָשָׁע֙ בַּל־לָמַ֣ד צֶ֔דֶק בְּאֶ֥רֶץ נְכֹח֖וֹת יְעַוֵּ֑ל וּבַל־יִרְאֶ֖ה גֵּא֥וּת יְהוָֽה׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: יְהוָ֛ה רָ֥מָה יָדְךָ֖ בַּל־יֶחֱזָי֑וּן יֶחֱז֤וּ וְיֵבֹ֙שׁוּ֙ קִנְאַת־עָ֔ם אַף־אֵ֖שׁ צָרֶ֥יךָ תֹאכְלֵֽם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: O YHWH, your hand is lifted high, yet they do not see it; let them see your zeal for the people and be ashamed; yea, let the fire kept for your adversaries consume them.
i18n.he: יְהוָ֛ה רָ֥מָה יָדְךָ֖ בַּל־יֶחֱזָי֑וּן יֶחֱז֤וּ וְיֵבֹ֙שׁוּ֙ קִנְאַת־עָ֔ם אַף־אֵ֖שׁ צָרֶ֥יךָ תֹאכְלֵֽם׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: יְהוָ֕ה תִּשְׁפֹּ֥ת שָׁל֖וֹם לָ֑נוּ כִּ֛י גַּ֥ם כָּֽל־מַעֲשֵׂ֖ינוּ פָּעַ֥לְתָּ לָּֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: O YHWH, you will establish peace for us, for you have also wrought all our works for us.
i18n.he: יְהוָ֕ה תִּשְׁפֹּ֥ת שָׁל֖וֹם לָ֑נוּ כִּ֛י גַּ֥ם כָּֽל־מַעֲשֵׂ֖ינוּ פָּעַ֥לְתָּ לָּֽנוּ׃

paragraphs.text: יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ בְּעָל֥וּנוּ אֲדֹנִ֖ים זֽוּלָתֶ֑ךָ לְבַד־בְּךָ֖ נַזְכִּ֥יר שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: O YHWH our God, other lords besides you have ruled over us; but by you alone do we make mention of your name.
i18n.he: יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ בְּעָל֥וּנוּ אֲדֹנִ֖ים זֽוּלָתֶ֑ךָ לְבַד־בְּךָ֖ נַזְכִּ֥יר שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

notes.official: Two decisions. *ʾĕlōhênû* 'our God' (suffixed *ʾĕlōhîm*) is rendered plainly; the corpus 'the Elohim' convention (central *elohim-as-translation*, scoped to Genesis 1) is deliberately NOT applied to a suffixed first-person confession, consistent with the non-applications at Isa 53:4, 24:15, and 25:1/25:9. *ʾăḏōnîm zûlāṯeḵā* 'other lords besides you' is the plural of *ʾāḏôn* 'lord, master' naming the human/foreign overlords who have ruled Judah (Assyria, Babylon) — NOT the divine title *ʾăḏōnāy* 'the Lord' — so no divine referent is imported; *bᵉʿālûnû* (*bʿl* 'rule, be master over') is 'have ruled over us' (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp).

paragraphs.text: מֵתִים֙ בַּל־יִחְי֔וּ רְפָאִ֖ים בַּל־יָקֻ֑מוּ לָכֵ֤ן פָּקַ֙דְתָּ֙ וַתַּשְׁמִידֵ֔ם וַתְּאַבֵּ֥ד כָּל־זֵ֖כֶר לָֽמוֹ׃

i18n.en: The dead do not live, the shades do not rise; therefore you have punished and destroyed them, and made all memory of them perish.
i18n.he: מֵתִים֙ בַּל־יִחְי֔וּ רְפָאִ֖ים בַּל־יָקֻ֑מוּ לָכֵ֤ן פָּקַ֙דְתָּ֙ וַתַּשְׁמִידֵ֔ם וַתְּאַבֵּ֥ד כָּל־זֵ֖כֶר לָֽמוֹ׃

notes.official: *Rᵉp̄āʾîm* here means 'the shades' — the powerless dead in Sheol (as at Isa 14:9; Ps 88:11; Prov 2:18; Job 26:5), NOT the giant-people Rephaim of Gen 14:5 / Deut 2–3 or the Ugaritic *rpʾum* (the divinized heroic dead). The lexeme is homonymous with, and etymologically entangled with, that giant-warrior sense — BDB and HALOT track them as one lemma — but the two form 'a separate philological track' (so the central *refaim-giant-peoples* entry's own rationale, which names 26:14 and 26:19 as the shades-sense); accordingly neither that entry nor the central *nephilim-giants-1-enoch-7-gen-6-4-cross-corpus* entry is applied here, since the dead 'other lords' of 26:13 are the ordinary dead, not warriors. 'The dead do not live, the shades do not rise' declares those overlords impotent — the deliberate inverse of 26:19, where YHWH's own dead DO rise and the earth gives up its shades alive (Wildberger; L'Heureux, *Rank Among the Canaanite Gods*, 1979; J. Day, *God's Conflict with the Dragon and the Sea*, 1985).

paragraphs.text: יָסַ֤פְתָּ לַגּוֹי֙ יְהוָ֔ה יָסַ֥פְתָּ לַגּ֖וֹי נִכְבָּ֑דְתָּ רִחַ֖קְתָּ כָּל־קַצְוֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: You have increased the nation, O YHWH, you have increased the nation; you are glorified; you have extended far all the borders of the land.
i18n.he: יָסַ֤פְתָּ לַגּוֹי֙ יְהוָ֔ה יָסַ֥פְתָּ לַגּ֖וֹי נִכְבָּ֑דְתָּ רִחַ֖קְתָּ כָּל־קַצְוֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

paragraphs.text: יְהוָ֖ה בַּצַּ֣ר פְּקָד֑וּךָ צָק֣וּן לַ֔חַשׁ מוּסָרְךָ֖ לָֽמוֹ׃

i18n.en: O YHWH, in distress they sought you; they poured out a whispered prayer when your chastening was upon them.
i18n.he: יְהוָ֖ה בַּצַּ֣ר פְּקָד֑וּךָ צָק֣וּן לַ֔חַשׁ מוּסָרְךָ֖ לָֽמוֹ׃

notes.official: The colon *ṣāqûn laḥaš* is textually hard. *Ṣāqûn* is an anomalous form best taken from *ṣûq* 'pour out, be in straits' ('they poured out'), and *laḥaš* is 'a whisper' — used of a hushed prayer or of a magical charm/incantation (Isa 3:3; Eccl 10:11; Ps 58:6). This translation reads 'they poured out a whispered prayer' (JPS 'silently they poured out a prayer'), the hushed-petition sense fitting Judah seeking YHWH 'in distress' under his chastening (*mûsārḵā*), against the 'charm/incantation' and 'cried out in a whisper' construals (Wildberger; Blenkinsopp; BDB, HALOT s.v. *laḥaš*).

paragraphs.text: כְּמ֤וֹ הָרָה֙ תַּקְרִ֣יב לָלֶ֔דֶת תָּחִ֥יל תִּזְעַ֖ק בַּחֲבָלֶ֑יהָ כֵּ֛ן הָיִ֥ינוּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: As a pregnant woman drawing near to give birth writhes and cries out in her pangs, so were we before you, O YHWH.
i18n.he: כְּמ֤וֹ הָרָה֙ תַּקְרִ֣יב לָלֶ֔דֶת תָּחִ֥יל תִּזְעַ֖ק בַּחֲבָלֶ֑יהָ כֵּ֛ן הָיִ֥ינוּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ יְהוָֽה׃

paragraphs.text: הָרִ֣ינוּ חַ֔לְנוּ כְּמ֖וֹ יָלַ֣דְנוּ ר֑וּחַ יְשׁוּעֹת֙ בַּל־נַ֣עֲשֶׂה אֶ֔רֶץ וּבַֽל־יִפְּל֖וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃

i18n.en: We conceived, we writhed; it was as if we gave birth to wind. We have wrought no deliverance in the earth, and the inhabitants of the world have not come to birth.
i18n.he: הָרִ֣ינוּ חַ֔לְנוּ כְּמ֖וֹ יָלַ֣דְנוּ ר֑וּחַ יְשׁוּעֹת֙ בַּל־נַ֣עֲשֶׂה אֶ֔רֶץ וּבַֽל־יִפְּל֖וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃

notes.official: The childbirth simile of 26:17 turns to failure: the people 'gave birth to wind' (*yāladnû rûaḥ*) — labor that produced nothing. *Yᵉšûʿōṯ bal-naʿăśeh ʾereṣ* is 'we have wrought no deliverance(s) in the earth' (*yᵉšûʿōṯ* plural). The obscure *û-ḇal yippᵉlû yōšᵉḇê ṯēḇēl* turns on *yippᵉlû* (*nāp̄al* 'fall'): either 'the inhabitants of the world have not fallen / been overthrown' (ASV) or, continuing the birth-metaphor, 'have not come to birth' (JPS); this translation takes the childbirth reading, consistent with the imagery of 26:17–19 and anticipating *tappîl* 'give birth' at 26:19, with the 'fall/overthrow' alternative noted (Wildberger; Kaiser, *Isaiah 13–39*, OTL).

paragraphs.text: יִֽחְי֣וּ מֵתֶ֔יךָ נְבֵלָתִ֖י יְקוּמ֑וּן הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר כִּ֣י טַ֤ל אוֹרֹת֙ טַלֶּ֔ךָ וָאָ֖רֶץ רְפָאִ֥ים תַּפִּֽיל׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Your dead shall live; my corpses shall rise. Awake and sing for joy, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth will give birth to the shades.
i18n.he: יִֽחְי֣וּ מֵתֶ֔יךָ נְבֵלָתִ֖י יְקוּמ֑וּן הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר כִּ֣י טַ֤ל אוֹרֹת֙ טַלֶּ֔ךָ וָאָ֖רֶץ רְפָאִ֥ים תַּפִּֽיל׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*Yiḥyû mēṯeḵā … yᵉqûmûn* 'Your dead shall live; my corpses shall rise' is the chapter's marquee line and the clearest resurrection-language in Isaiah. The Masoretic surface is rendered plainly — 'your dead shall live' is grammatically explicit — while whether the raising is literal individual bodily resurrection or a national/corporate-restoration metaphor (the dead nation revived, as in Ezekiel's dry bones) is left open, not pre-resolved. The bodily-resurrection reading and the cross-corpus link belong to the interpretive layer: Dan 12:2 (the Hebrew Bible's first unambiguous individual-eschatological resurrection) and Ezek 37 (the corporate dry-bones resurrection) are the companion witnesses, and the central *resurrection-dan-12-2-3-foundational-cross-corpus* entry — whose own source-note names Isa 26:19 'the prophetic-resurrection fountainhead' — is extended to govern this verse (its lens-discipline keeps the corporate/individual question open).

*Nᵉḇēlāṯî* is formally 1cs singular 'my corpse' (*nᵉḇēlāh* 'carcass, corpse') but pairs with the 3mp *yᵉqûmûn* 'they shall arise'; it is rendered collectively 'my corpses shall rise', retaining the Masoretic text against the widely-proposed emendation *nᵉḇēlāṯām* 'their bodies' (NRSV/RSV).

*Ṭal ʾôrōṯ* 'a dew of lights' reads *ʾôrōṯ* as the plural of *ʾôrāh* 'light' (a luminous, life-giving dew that quickens those who 'dwell in the dust'), against the homograph *ʾôrōṯ* 'herbs, mallows' (a dew that revives vegetation, ASV/KJV 'dew of herbs'); the 'lights' reading is kept and the 'herbs' reading disclosed.

*Rᵉp̄āʾîm* returns from 26:14, again the 'shades' — but here the earth gives them up ALIVE, the exact inverse of 26:14 where 'the shades do not rise'; still the underworld dead, NOT the giant-Rephaim. *Tappîl* (Hiphil of *nāp̄al*) is rendered 'the earth will give birth to the shades', tying the verb to the childbirth-imagery of 26:17–18 (so NRSV 'give birth'; JPS 'bring to life'), with the ASV/KJV 'cast forth / cast out' (the earth or Sheol disgorging its dead) as the equal alternative (J. Day, *God's Conflict with the Dragon and the Sea*, 1985; J. D. Levenson, *Resurrection and the Restoration of Israel*, 2006; Wildberger, *Isaiah 13–27*; Blenkinsopp, *Isaiah 1–39*).

paragraphs.text: לֵ֤ךְ עַמִּי֙ בֹּ֣א בַחֲדָרֶ֔יךָ וּֽסְגֹ֥ר דלתיך [דְּלָתְךָ֖] בַּעֲדֶ֑ךָ חֲבִ֥י כִמְעַט־רֶ֖גַע עַד־יעבור־[יַעֲבָר־] זָֽעַם׃

i18n.en: Come, my people, enter your chambers and shut your door behind you; hide yourself for a little moment, until the indignation passes over.
i18n.he: לֵ֤ךְ עַמִּי֙ בֹּ֣א בַחֲדָרֶ֔יךָ וּֽסְגֹ֥ר דלתיך [דְּלָתְךָ֖] בַּעֲדֶ֑ךָ חֲבִ֥י כִמְעַט־רֶ֖גַע עַד־יעבור־[יַעֲבָר־] זָֽעַם׃

notes.official: Two ketiv/qere pairs. The consonantal ketiv *dᵉlāṯeḵā* 'your doors' (plural) is read by the qere as *dᵉlāṯḵā* 'your door' (singular); the ketiv *yaʿăḇôr* is read by the qere as *yaʿăḇār* 'passes'. Per the project's structural-preservation convention the qere is translated ('shut your door behind you … until the indignation passes over') and the ketiv is preserved in the source and noted; the differences are orthographic/morphological and non-substantive. *ḥăḇî* 'hide yourself' and *zaʿam* 'indignation, wrath' frame the summons to the people to shelter 'for a little moment' until YHWH's wrath — the wrath that falls on the earth's inhabitants in 26:21 — has passed over (cf. the Passover sheltering, Exod 12:22–23; Wildberger; Blenkinsopp).

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יֹצֵ֣א מִמְּקוֹמ֔וֹ לִפְקֹ֛ד עֲוֺ֥ן יֹֽשֵׁב־הָאָ֖רֶץ עָלָ֑יו וְגִלְּתָ֤ה הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ אֶת־דָּמֶ֔יהָ וְלֹֽא־תְכַסֶּ֥ה ע֖וֹד עַל־הֲרוּגֶֽיהָ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For behold, YHWH is coming out from his place to punish the iniquity of the inhabitant of the earth against him; and the earth shall disclose her blood and no longer cover over her slain.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יֹצֵ֣א מִמְּקוֹמ֔וֹ לִפְקֹ֛ד עֲוֺ֥ן יֹֽשֵׁב־הָאָ֖רֶץ עָלָ֑יו וְגִלְּתָ֤ה הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ אֶת־דָּמֶ֔יהָ וְלֹֽא־תְכַסֶּ֥ה ע֖וֹד עַל־הֲרוּגֶֽיהָ׃ (ס)

notes.official: The theophany: *YHWH yōṣēʾ mimmᵉqômô* 'YHWH is coming out from his place' — the deity leaving his dwelling to execute judgment (cf. Mic 1:3). *ʿăwōn* 'iniquity' is rendered per the central *avon-iniquity-cross-corpus-keyword* entry (appliesTo extended to ISA-26:21), the corpus's principal sin-vocabulary lexeme; *pqd* 'visit / punish'. *wᵉgillᵉṯāh hā-ʾāreṣ ʾeṯ-dāmehā* 'the earth shall disclose her blood(s)' pictures the ground uncovering the shed blood it had absorbed so that the slain (*hărûgehā*) are no longer hidden and the bloodguilt can be avenged (cf. Gen 4:10–11, the ground opening its mouth for Abel's blood; Job 16:18). Rendered plainly, no lens (Wildberger, *Isaiah 13–27*; Blenkinsopp, *Isaiah 1–39*).
